meaning: a person carried away by excessive and uncritical zeal for a cause, creed or pastime
sentence: A cricket fanatic, he had not missed a home match in eleven years.

meaning: at or to a greater physical distance; the comparative used of measurable space
sentence: The second checkpoint lay farther down the ridge than the map suggested.

meaning: praising someone more warmly than is sincere or deserved; also showing a person to advantage
sentence: The photograph was flattering, but everyone recognised her at once.

meaning: to disobey a rule, law or custom openly and with contempt
sentence: Shopkeepers who flout the fire regulations will lose their licence.

meaning: to hold back patiently from doing something one could well have done
sentence: She could not forbear from laughing when the parade went wrong.

meaning: an ancestor; a person from whom one is descended
sentence: His forebears had farmed the same valley for two centuries.

meaning: a short introductory note printed at the front of a book, usually written by someone other than the author
sentence: The general wrote a brief foreword to the regimental history.

meaning: towards the front or the time ahead; as a verb, to send something on to a further address
sentence: She stepped forward and asked the office to forward her letters to the new posting.

meaning: the quality of being easily broken, damaged or upset
sentence: The fragility of the truce became obvious within a week.

meaning: fast and energetic in a wild, uncontrolled way
sentence: The last hour before the inspection was frenetic.

meaning: a state of wild, uncontrolled excitement or agitation
sentence: News of the transfer sent the whole barracks into a frenzy.

meaning: to a greater extent or degree, or additional in amount; as a verb, to help something advance
sentence: He said nothing further at the meeting, though the posting would certainly further his career.

meaning: pointlessness; the quality of producing no useful result
sentence: After the third failed attempt he saw the futility of arguing.

meaning: cheerful, lively high spirits; also brightness or showiness of appearance
sentence: The gaiety of the mess dinner carried on well past midnight.

meaning: a person's or an animal's manner of walking or running
sentence: You could recognise the havildar at a distance by his stiff, deliberate gait.

meaning: a hinged or sliding barrier that closes an opening in a wall, fence or boundary
sentence: The sentry swung the gate open for the convoy.

meaning: showy but cheaply made and worthless; as a noun, such a flimsy trinket
sentence: The stalls sold gimcrack souvenirs that fell apart on the bus home.

meaning: moving or formed with smooth, pleasing elegance; also showing tact and good manners
sentence: Her dive was graceful enough to draw applause from the bank.

meaning: the degree of slope of a road, railway or surface; also the rate at which a quantity changes over a distance
sentence: The lorry laboured up a gradient of one in eight.

meaning: a sum of money given for service, whether as a tip or as a lump sum paid to an employee on retirement
sentence: He received a gratuity along with his pension on retiring from the regiment.

meaning: a formal promise that something will be done or will meet a stated standard, with an undertaking to put it right or to answer for another's obligation if it is not
sentence: The contractor gave a five-year guarantee against leaks, and his brother stood guarantee for the loan.

meaning: frozen rain falling as pellets of ice; as a verb, to call out to or acclaim someone
sentence: Hail battered the tents overnight, and in the morning the villagers came out to hail the rescue party.

meaning: free of illness, strong and vigorous, especially in old age
sentence: At eighty-two he was still hale enough to walk to the market and back.

meaning: full of frantic and incessant activity
sentence: The week before the board examination was hectic.

meaning: the traditions, buildings, customs or qualities handed down from earlier generations
sentence: The fort was restored as part of the state's heritage.

meaning: something that makes progress or action difficult; an obstacle
sentence: The narrow track proved a hindrance to the ambulance.

meaning: important enough to be remembered in history; famous or momentous
sentence: The signing of the accord was a historic moment for the valley.

meaning: belonging to or concerned with the past and its records, whether or not it was of any importance
sentence: She checked the historical records for the regiment's first posting.

meaning: having an empty space inside instead of being solid; also insincere and worthless
sentence: A hollow log lay across the stream, and his promise to repair the bridge proved equally hollow.

meaning: a large and usually disorderly crowd of people moving together
sentence: A horde of ticketless fans pushed at the gate.
